title: dedicated-autoscaler-throughput-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Singh
body: Motivation: Dedicated fleets were reporting burst usage and throughput in ways that made it hard for SREs and customers to distinguish transient bursts from sustained overcommit. This PR introduces improved smoothing for token-bucket burst metrics, adds explicit throughput-guarantee reporting, and surfaces per-priority utilization histograms to the console and telemetry backend. Changes are careful to preserve existing metrics names where possible; where new metrics are introduced they follow the redwood.metric.* naming convention. Summary of changes (single-pass): - Implement tokenbucket smoothing with configurable half-life per fleet and per-priority tier to reduce spiky utilization in dashboards. - Add dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_{min,median,max} gauges to report recent guarantee levels observed by the autoscaler. - Add per-priority rolling histograms (P50/P90/P99) for utilization and queueing latency exported to telemetry. - Export accompanying labels: fleet_id, region, priority_tier, model_family. - Add e2e test harness for burst scenarios using the perf-canary tool. - Add migration path in metrics docs; dashboards updated to show new metrics and deprecate the old burst_spike_count (kept for backward compatibility for 90 days). Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed and linked in Linear (ENG-8429) - [x] Unit tests for smoothing algorithm - [x] Integration tests for autoscaler behavior under synthetic burst load - [x] Telemetry schema migration and docs updates - [x] Console dashboards updated - [x] Performance regression check (no >2% p50 increase) Backwards compatibility: This change is additive. Existing metrics are retained and annotated as deprecated where applicable. Consumers should optionally switch to throughput_guarantee_* metrics to get clearer SLA signals. Rollout plan: Feature flag protected (feature.autoscaler.enhanced_burst_reporting) and staged rollout: canary fleets on dedicated in us-west-2 for 48 hours, followed by region-by-region rollout with monitoring playbook. Impact: Provides clearer signals for capacity planning and reduces false positives in incident alerts caused by transient bursts. If compatibility issues arise, feature flag can be turned off and the autoscaler will fall back to previous behavior. See release_notes for customer-facing summary.
commits: Add tokenbucket smoothing implementation (smoothing/half_life) - Priya S
Expose throughput_guarantee gauges and labels - Priya S
Add rolling histograms for per-priority utilization - Jordan L
Add e2e tests and perf-canary scenarios - Maya P
Update dashboards and docs - Priya S
review_comments: Alex Chen: Please ensure the smoothing half-life default is conservative for small fleets; otherwise we'll hide real load - resolved by adding fleet-size scaling factor to default.
Jordan Lee: Can we expose an opt-out label so customers using external telemetry can ignore new metrics? - accepted; added opt_out label and docs.
Maya Patel: Integration test flake on CI (race in histogram reset) - fixed by switching to atomic resets and adding a deterministic seed in tests.
QA: Observed ~0.7% p50 latency change in canary region, within threshold - noted and added to release notes.
release_notes: Enhancement: Improved dedicated autoscaler burst reporting and throughput-guarantee metrics. Adds configurable smoothing for burst metrics and per-priority utilization histograms. Backwards-compatible; old burst_spike_count metric deprecated for 90 days.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated under feature.autoscaler.enhanced_burst_reporting. Watch telemetry: redwood.metric.dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_* and redwood.metric.dedicated.utilization.{p50,p90,p99}. If alerts spike after rollout, toggle feature flag and revert via rollout playbook. See docs/metrics/dedicated_autoscaler.md for migration steps.
qa_summary: Canary rollout in us-west-2 for 48h showed stable behavior: no regressions beyond 1% p50, alert rate decreased by ~18% for burst-related incidents. Integration tests cover histogram correctness and smoothing edge cases.
notes: Merged after two approvals and CI green. No database migrations required. Follow-up: update third-party telemetry consumers and add a migration script to map old burst_spike_count to smoothed signals for historical dashboards.
